reasoning: I found nothing that stops a huge utilization value between the decoder and the Int(Double) trap. (1) Source: AnthropicWireTypes.swift:71 reads utilization with flexibleDoubleIfPresent. That function (AppConfig.swift:199-203) returns any decoded Double, with no range or finiteness check. (2) Nothing in between: toSnapshot (AnthropicWireTypes.swift:140-185) passes the value straight to UsageWindow, and UsageWindow.init (UsageWindow.swift:15-23) stores it unchanged. The only comment there says 'or higher if the vendor reports overuse', so large values are expected. VendorSnapshot.maxUtilization (UsageSnapshot.swift:70-72) takes a plain max(). UsageStore.swift:379 folds it in with only an 'm > maxUtil' comparison. The only isFinite guard nearby is UsageSnapshot.swift:325, which is a different predicate. The isFinite guards in CreditBaseline apply to credits, not to plan windows. (3) Sink: the default menuBarMode is .iconAndPercent (AppConfig.swift:230), and MenuBarLabelView.swift:41 runs Text("\(Int(percent.rounded()))%"). Swift's Int(Double) crashes the app when the value is out of range, and the same conversion appears at ProviderRowView.swift:26 and PinnedStatusItemManager.swift:97/100/110. Neither the framework nor the type system prevents it: JSONDecoder accepts 1e300 as a valid finite Double. One limit: the attacker would have to be Anthropic's API itself (a malicious or compromised vendor), since TLS blocks an ordinary man-in-the-middle. That limits how often this can happen, but it is not a defense, and the finding already lists it as a precondition.
